prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits via transformer/feeder bays. Automation boundary: bay monitoring/control, station coordination, external interfaces; primary equipment, protection and field wiring stay under approved designs/limits. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) does bay sequencing, status evaluation, permissive checks, produces Bay Status Digest, requests breaker operations from Breaker Control Unit only when mode/permissives allow. North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller automate their station portions. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) gives local feeder protection independent of supervisory availability, uses approved setting group (pickups, delays, logic), produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized operations, enforces authoritative local interlocks. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): operator interface, supervisory coordination, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; no protective functions. Station Gateway: boundary for authorized external/remote communications. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) distributes time, produces Clock Drift Snapshot when offset meets reporting condition; holdover degrades on reference loss. Sequence Event Archive retains events. Engineering Workstation keeps configuration under revision control, retains approved configuration/history with access limited to assigned engineering personnel, produces Settings Review Receipt after settings review. Maintenance Remote Terminal: approved maintenance access only. Station DC System supplies control power; loss can interrupt visibility/timing. Actors: Control Room Operator directs operation, coordinates access with Switching Desk Coordinator before work affecting energized equipment; Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) develops/documents setting changes against approved study, verifies coordination, records approval status before release; second qualified reviewer independently checks; Substation Field Crew (Cinder) does inspections, maintenance, switching support, setting transfer per authorized instructions after work authorization/site entry confirmed; Substation Supervisor ensures authorization/control process. Requirements: protection independent of bay control; local control precedence; remote commands subject to permissions/interlocks; unique revision ID before review; no approval from copied values; coordination checks up/downstream; pre-deployment model/firmware check; approved work window if protection affected; post-install comparison and functional check; discrepancy halts release until resolved/reviewed. Stale data after comms loss must be confirmed; timestamps don't validate measurements.

New part:
S078: The Substation Supervisor confirms that the requested work is consistent with current operating conditions and approved procedures.
S079: The crew reviews the work scope, access route, known hazards, and communication arrangements before entering the yard.
S080: Personnel use the site access process to record arrival and departure so that the control room can account for field staff.
S081: Work boundaries are established before tools or test equipment are brought near electrical apparatus.
S082: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the applicable switching and clearance arrangements before work begins.
S083: The Control Room Operator retains authority to suspend work when operating conditions change or indications become uncertain.
S084: The Substation Field Crew verifies equipment identity at the point of work against the approved work documentation.
S085: Field personnel do not rely on screen indications alone to establish that equipment is safe to approach or handle.
S086: Required checks of position, isolation, and absence of hazardous energy are performed using approved site procedures.
S087: Any discrepancy between field observations and control-room indications is treated as an unsafe condition until resolved.
S088: The crew promptly reports uncertain equipment conditions through the designated operational communication channel.
S089: Substation Field Crew completes and sends the Breaker Inspection Tag after recording the observed breaker condition and inspection time.
S090: The Station Supervisory Control System presents available equipment indications for operator review during normal operation.
S091: The Bay Automation Controller applies configured permissives and interlocks to supported automated operations.
S092: Automation does not replace field verification when a procedure requires direct confirmation of equipment condition.
S093: The Control Room Operator evaluates reported field conditions before authorizing a return to automated operation.
S094: Field crews maintain communications with the control room throughout work that could affect protection, control, or service continuity.
S095: If communications are lost, the crew stops affected work and follows the approved hold and escalation procedure.
S096: Work is considered complete only after personnel, tools, and temporary connections are accounted for and the work area is left in a safe state.
S097: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms the operational handback arrangements before equipment is returned to service.
S098: The Sequence Event Archive is the station's authoritative repository for time-stamped operational event evidence.
S099: The Sequence Event Archive is known operationally as Orchard.
S100: It preserves event records in their received form so later review does not depend on transient operator displays.
S101: Each retained record includes its source identity, event time, archive receipt time, and available quality indications.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
